en.title: Lilly Wachowski Still Fighting to Adapt Cyberpunk Novel 'Bang Bang Bodhisattva'
en.summary: The visionary filmmaker behind The Matrix has been actively pursuing an adaptation of Aubrey Wood's acclaimed 2023 novel. Despite facing significant hurdles, both creator and director remain committed to bringing the story to the screen.
en.body:
## A Passion Project Persists

Despite recent setbacks in her production endeavors, **Lilly Wachowski** has not abandoned her ambition to adapt **Aubrey Wood**'s celebrated 2023 cyberpunk novel, **Bang Bang Bodhisattva**. Author Aubrey Wood recently confirmed on Bluesky that Wachowski personally optioned the rights to the novel for a feature film shortly after its release, funding the acquisition entirely out of her own pocket.

While the project initially faced significant development issues, reportedly falling apart around the same time Wachowski's planned adaptation of Gretchen Felker-Martin's *Manhunt* was also shelved, the creative spark between Wood and Wachowski clearly remains. Wood alluded that these production challenges might stem from similar reasons impacting other projects, potentially including Wachowski's stated commitment to a "wall-to-wall trans cast" for her political thriller film *The Hunted*, which has also struggled to gain traction.

> "I have the go-ahead to talk about this finally. Lilly Wachowski optioned Bang Bang Bodhisattva for a feature film soon after its release, paying for the rights out of her own pocket. Unfortunately the project fell apart right around the same time the Manhunt show was canned, for similar reasons." — **Aubrey Wood**

## The Hurdles of a Hostile Market

The path for ambitious, creator-driven projects in Hollywood can be fraught with obstacles, and **Bang Bang Bodhisattva** appears to be no exception. Wood acknowledged that while she and Wachowski are still keen to collaborate on the adaptation in the future, the current industry climate is "hostile." This sentiment likely reflects broader challenges in securing funding and navigating studio politics for projects that push creative boundaries or diverge from established commercial formulas. The success of **Bang Bang Bodhisattva** as a novel, however, serves as a testament to its strong narrative and thematic resonance, suggesting that audience appetite for such stories exists, even if the market is slow to respond.

## What's Next for Bang Bang Bodhisattva

While a definitive timeline for the **Bang Bang Bodhisattva** adaptation remains uncertain, the continued interest from **Lilly Wachowski** and the author's encouragement for continued reader support offer a hopeful outlook. Wood emphasized that ongoing engagement with her work could bolster the chances of this cinematic vision coming to fruition. Fans eager to see this cyberpunk tale on the big screen are encouraged to continue supporting Aubrey Wood's literary endeavors, as this collective enthusiasm may prove crucial in overcoming the current market challenges.

Unfortunately the project fell apart right around the same time the Manhunt show was canned, for similar reasons.” Wood seems to be referring to Wachowski’s attempt to adapt Gretchen Felker-Martin’s Manhunt novel into a TV series. While there has been no official word regarding that project’s status recently, Wachowski did recently say that she can’t get her political thriller film The Hunted going because of her insistence on a “wall-to-wall trans cast.” It’s possible that Wachowski’s other recent projects have faced similar production hurdles. Wood does go on to note that she and Wachowski are still interested in working together on this project down the line but that the “market is hostile” at the moment. She encourages people to continue to support her work in order to increase the chances of that adaptation ever happening. The author shared this information in response to a fan who shared a 2023 quote from Wachowski in which the director said that she is increasingly focused on supporting and mentoring “up-and-coming trans talent.” If you’re unfamiliar with Bang Bang Bodhisattva , the novel follows a futuristic gig worker who navigates a noir murder mystery with the help of a private investigator she sometimes works with. The story has been praised for its writing, futuristic world-building, and incorporation of noir storytelling into a cyberpunk setting that utilizes and challenges the ideas of both genres. Perhaps you can see why Lilly Wachowski might be so interested in this project and why many believe she’d be a perfect fit for the material. There is some good news on the Lilly Wachowski project front, though. It was recently announced that Wachowski will produce Cassie Workman Is Witchy AF : an upcoming eight-part YouTube comedy documentary series starring Cassie Workman that explores the history of various aspects of the occult. Described as a show “created in a lab specifically to make Ron DeSantis angry,” it sounds like it’ll be more than worth a watch when it debuts on September 16.[end-mark] The post Lilly Wachowski Still Wants to Adapt <i>Bang Bang
